thread:
nate: Quick sync — I'm seeing bursty tail latency when pages are offloaded between host pools across nodes. Repro on staging with concurrent workloads. Anyone else hit this?

lucas: Yup, hit it this morning. Pattern: node-A starts staging a chunk to node-B while node-B is running compaction/evict loop. Result: stalled RPCs and a couple of requests re-fetching pages -> tail spike.

sophia: Can you paste a short log snippet?

lucas: sure:
```
[evict] 2026-02-18T09:12:03.123Z nodeA -> nodeB chunk=0x7f9a stall=930ms
[compact] 2026-02-18T09:12:03.220Z nodeB compaction loop pause=120ms
[fetch] 2026-02-18T09:12:04.120Z page miss, fallback to disk, ttl=12ms
```

maria: That matches an anomaly from the residency sampler: cross-node migration_latency percentile jumps when compaction duty is high. Also saw some refcount deltas not matching after rapid migrate+evict sequences.

nate: So two problems smell related: (1) ordering/coordination when a page moves while other housekeeping runs, (2) fragmentation/compaction interference making staging slower. Need to decide interface boundaries: who is authoritative for a page residency record during migration?

sophia: Current model: origin node issues migration request, target node accepts and writes a transient residency entry, then origin clears. But there's a race where the target's compaction may evict the incoming chunk before migration finishes, and our retry logic makes origin retry which causes duplicate refcount ops.

lucas: Right — we see refcount underflows in logs followed by quick compensating increments. Two approaches:
- strong handoff: lock/lease page during migration (serializes operations, simpler correctness)
- optimistic handoff: migration-id + reconcile pass (faster, more concurrent, needs robust reconciliation)

maria: Performance-wise, strong handoff will add latency on the critical path for hot pages. Optimistic needs a compact reconciliation flow that can run off the hot path. Tradeoff: latency vs implementation complexity and edge-case correctness.

sophia: Another axis: where to run compaction? If compaction runs with awareness of incoming migrations (backpressure signal), it can avoid evicting staging writes. But that requires cross-node signaling or a small lease token that marks an incoming page as "do not compact" for N ms.

nate: I sketched a strawman: give each migration a short lease token (migration-lease-ms config), target marks incoming page with lease, compaction checks lease and skips if active. If lease expires and page not finalized, target either aborts or reconciles. That keeps latency low and avoids global locks.

sophia: Lease length tuning is tricky. Short lease -> more aborts/retries; long lease -> more memory pinned during slow networks. Could make lease adaptive based on network RTT and chunk size.

lucas: Also need metrics: migration_conflicts, migration_aborts, lease_renewals, cross_node_stage_latency. Please add before we flip any defaults.

maria: On fragmentation: compaction currently targets local fragmentation ratio threshold. But when cross-node staging is common, compaction aggressiveness should be aware of incoming migration rate. Maybe degrade compaction frequency if incoming_migrations/sec > threshold.

infra-bot: Reminder: test cluster "staging-gpu-5" will be drained tomorrow 03:00 UTC for infra updates.

nate: Good to know. Action items I propose:
1) I will open an RFC for a "migration-lease" protocol describing fields: migration_id, lease_ms, state=(init, in-flight, committed, aborted), and reconciliation flow.
2) lucas: add the metrics maria listed and a small debug log category for migration lifecycle.
3) sophia: experiment with adaptive lease tuning on staging with a range (100ms -> 1s) and report abort vs commit rates.
4) maria: propose compaction-scheduling heuristic to back off when incoming_migrations/sec > X.

lucas: ACK, I'll add metrics and a short dashboard.

sophia: ACK, will run a 24h experiment and post results.

maria: I'll mock a compaction policy patch and link in the RFC.

nate: Thanks. If the RFC lands today let's aim to validate on staging after infra window. Also note we should avoid adding a global coordinator — prefer per-node leases + reconciliation.

sophia: one more thought: make the reconciliation idempotent and include snapshot checksums so we can fast-fail migrations that conflict with compaction changes.

lucas: +1 to idempotent ops. Also add a small debug endpoint to list active migration leases per node.

maria: I'll add a gating test that simulates compaction+migration thundering to catch refcount races.

nate: Cool — I'll draft the RFC and ping y'all. Thanks! :thumbsup:
